key_insight: MemLens makes LLM agent memory smarter by deciding which interaction records are actually worth keeping, instead of treating all memories equally. This helps agents retain high-value information for better long-horizon reasoning and personalization.
problem_solved: Existing LLM memory systems often store heterogeneous user-agent interaction records in a coarse, utility-agnostic way, which leads to redundant, low-impact, or noisy memories occupying limited storage and reducing retrieval quality.
method: Introduces a value-aware memory management framework for LLM-based agents.
Assigns different importance to interaction records based on their utility for future reasoning, reuse, and personalization.
Provides interactive analytics to help users inspect, understand, and manage memory contents more effectively.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, MemLens can improve agent reliability, memory efficiency, and response quality by keeping the most useful information accessible. It also adds transparency and control, making memory systems easier to debug and tune in real deployments.
visual_elements: A memory pipeline diagram showing record capture, value scoring, pruning, and retrieval.
A before-vs-after memory store visualization comparing coarse-grained storage with value-aware selection.
An interactive dashboard mockup with filters, rankings, and memory analytics icons.
A bar chart or heatmap showing memory item utility, retention, and redundancy reduction.
paper_title: MemLens: A Value-Aware Memory Management System with Interactive Analytics for LLM-based Agents
paper_authors: Shuyue Wei, Chang Liu, Zimu Zhou, Yongxin Tong, Lizhen Cui
